options.text: An intermediary in front of servers that receives client requests on their behalf
An intermediary in front of clients that forwards their outbound requests
A DNS server that caches records
A tool that assigns IP addresses

questions.explanation: A reverse proxy fronts servers and receives requests for them. A proxy that fronts clients and forwards their requests is a forward proxy.

questions.prompt: Which capability requires a Layer 7 (not Layer 4) load balancer?

options.text: Routing /api requests to one pool and /images to another
Forwarding a TCP connection by destination port
Balancing UDP by IP and port

questions.explanation: Routing by URL path requires reading HTTP, which is a Layer 7 feature. Layer 4 balances by IP/port without inspecting content.

questions.prompt: A load balancer removes a failed backend from rotation automatically based on a periodic probe called a ____.
questions.explanation: Health checks probe each backend (e.g. GET /health); unhealthy servers are removed and re-added when they recover.

questions.prompt: Match each load-balancing algorithm to its behavior.

pairs.right: Each request to the next server in turn
To the server with the fewest active connections
Same client IP always to the same server
Bigger servers get proportionally more traffic

questions.explanation: Round-robin alternates, least-connections adapts to load, IP hash gives stickiness, and weighted accounts for capacity.

questions.prompt: Which are common jobs of a reverse proxy? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Reverse proxies terminate TLS, balance load, and handle caching/compression/rate-limiting. DHCP leasing is unrelated.

questions.prompt: Order what happens when a backend crashes behind a load balancer with health checks.

items.text: The backend stops passing its health check
The load balancer removes it from rotation
Remaining healthy backends serve all traffic
When it recovers and passes checks, it is re-added

questions.explanation: A failing check removes the backend, healthy servers absorb the load, and recovery re-adds it — keeping users unaffected.
